2. The facts as stated in the writ petition, in short, are that the schedule land comprising 1.58 acres of Mouza Baro Ashulia, Savar, Dhaka and other lands belonged to Kali Kamal Roy Munshi @ Kali Proshanny Munshi and the said land was recorded as CS Plot No.1032 in CS Khatian No.319 in his name as a settled raiyat thereof and in continuance in possession thereof he passed away leaving behind his wife Labonny Prova Roy Munshi, three sons, namely, Poresh Nath Roy Munshi, Fatik Chandra Roy Munshi and Monindra Chandra Roy Munshi and their names were entered in attested SA Khatian No.319 and final SA Khatian copy of which could not be traced out from the concerned record room as the relevant page of the concerned volume was rent. 

 3. By amicable arrangement amongst the heirs and successors of the said Proshonny Kumar Roy Munshi his son Sree Monindra Chandra. Roy Munshi got the entire land of the aforesaid CS Plot No.1032 and being in possession thereof he transferred the said land and other lands by a registered deed of sale No.2703 dated 27-2-1961 to three brothers, namely, Hashim Uddin Ahmed, Momtaz Uddin Ahmed and Mofiz Uddin Ahmed and delivered possession thereof to the vendees, but in the deed Hashim Uddin Ahmed was shown to be the recipient and the jot entered 1.50 acres of land in place of 1.58 acres. The land of the plot in reference was endorsed in RS Khatian No.362 as RS Plot No.3168 in the name of the said Hashim Uddin Ahmed and his two brothers, namely, Momtaz Uddin Ahmed and Mofizuddin Ahmed. Momtaz Uddin Ahmed died leaving behind two wives Nur Jahan Begum, Dud Meher Begum, two sons, Md Nazrul Islam, Md Tajul Islam and one dauthter Rawshan Ara Akter. Mofizuddin, Hashim Uddin and the heirs of Momtazuddin partition their joint properties including the aforesaid land by a registered deed of partition No.23293 dated 12-11-1984 in consequence of which the aforesaid Hashim Uddin got entire 1.58 acres of land of the aforesaid plot in his exclusive saham and he continued to possess the same exclusively. Hashim Uddin Ahmed by a registered deed No.8503 dated 26-6-1990 transferred 1.50 acres of land of the plot in reference for good and valuable consideration to the petitioner and delivered possession thereof. The petitioner got his name mutated in SA records of right and obtained Mutation Khatian No.390/kat, Duplicate carbon receipt and rent receipt in the year 1993. In the middle of 1997 the respondent No.5 started pilling the land as described in the schedule below and while the petitioner demanded to know the cause thereof the respondents said that for making Tongi-Ashulia-Zirabo-EPZ road Government acquired the land of the petitioner and other lands through LA Cse No. 6/95-96 under the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982. Thus the petitioner gave a representation on 14-10-1998 to the land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka accompanied with all relevant documents stating that the respondents did not serve any notice under section 6 of the said Ordinance and requesting the Land Acquisition Officer to serve upon him a notice under section 7 of the said Ordinance. In the meantime the respondent completed construction of the aforesaid road through the plot in reference and extending the land dividing the entire plots into three pieces two of which on the road sides became unfit to use. 

 10. The respondent No.7—Executive Engineer, Dhaka Sarak Bibhag submitting an affidavit-in-opposition denied all the material aspect of the writ petition and claimed that the petitioner in this writ petition described CS, SA and RS Khatian and also registered sale deed having annexed therein are matter of saham, title, possession and ownership which are question of civil disputes and all these question have to be tested, examined and confirmed by the competent civil court.
